title: Joshua Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 17.

questions.question: Who was Manasseh described as in relation to Joseph?
options: The youngest son of Joseph
The firstborn of Joseph
A servant of Joseph
Joseph's brother
questions.correctAnswer: The firstborn of Joseph
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:1 states that Manasseh was the firstborn of Joseph.

questions.question: Why did Machir receive Gilead and Bashan?
options: Because he was a man of peace
Because he was a man of war
Because he was the youngest son
Because he was a priest
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was a man of war
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:1 explains that Machir had Gilead and Bashan because he was a man of war.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT listed as one of the families of Manasseh?
options: Children of Abiezer
Children of Helek
Children of Asriel
Children of Levi
questions.correctAnswer: Children of Levi
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:2 lists the families of Manasseh and does not include the children of Levi.

questions.question: How many daughters did Zelophehad have?
options: Three
Four
Five
Two
questions.correctAnswer: Five
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:3 names five daughters of Zelophehad: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

questions.question: Before whom did Zelophehad's daughters present their claim for inheritance?
options: Joshua and Eleazar the priest
Moses and Aaron
The king of Israel
The elders of Manasseh
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua and Eleazar the priest
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:4 states they came before Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the princes.

questions.question: How many portions fell to Manasseh besides the land of Gilead and Bashan?
options: Five
Ten
Twenty
Seven
questions.correctAnswer: Ten
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:5 mentions that ten portions fell to Manasseh besides Gilead and Bashan.

questions.question: True or False: The daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:6 confirms that the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons.

questions.question: True or False: The rest of Manasseh's sons had the land of Gilead.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:6 states the rest of Manasseh's sons had the land of Gilead.

questions.question: Which tribe's border stretched from Asher to Michmethah before Shechem?
options: Ephraim
Manasseh
Judah
Levi
questions.correctAnswer: Manasseh
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:7 says the coast of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethah before Shechem.

questions.question: True or False: Tappuah belonged to the children of Manasseh exclusively.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:8 clarifies that Tappuah on Manasseh's border belonged to the children of Ephraim.

questions.question: What did the children of Joseph say to Joshua about their inheritance?
options: They were satisfied with one lot
They asked for two lots
They complained about receiving only one lot and one portion
They wanted no inheritance
questions.correctAnswer: They complained about receiving only one lot and one portion
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:14 records the children of Joseph asking why they had only one lot and portion despite being a great people.

questions.question: What did Joshua suggest the children of Joseph do if the land of Mount Ephraim was too narrow?
options: Move to the desert
Cut down the wood country in the land of the Perizzites and giants
Ask for more land from the other tribes
Conquer the land of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Cut down the wood country in the land of the Perizzites and giants
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:15 tells them to cut down the wood country in the land of the Perizzites and giants if the mountain was too narrow.

questions.question: What did the children of Joseph say about the hill and the Canaanites living in the valleys?
options: The hill was large enough for them
The hill was not enough and the Canaanites had iron chariots
The Canaanites were too weak to fight
They wanted to live peacefully with the Canaanites
questions.correctAnswer: The hill was not enough and the Canaanites had iron chariots
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:16 records their complaint that the hill was insufficient and the Canaanites had iron chariots.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua told the house of Joseph they would only receive one lot.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:17 states that Joshua told them they would not have only one lot because they were a great people with power.

questions.question: What was promised to the children of Joseph concerning the mountain land?
options: They would share it with the Canaanites
They would not receive any of it
The mountain would be theirs if they cut down the wood and drove out the Canaanites
They would only receive the valleys
questions.correctAnswer: The mountain would be theirs if they cut down the wood and drove out the Canaanites
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:18 says the mountain would be theirs if they cut down the wood and drove out the Canaanites despite their iron chariots.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What geographical feature formed the northern border of Manasseh's inheritance according to Joshua 17?
options: The sea
The Jordan River
The river Kanah
The mountain of Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: The sea
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:9-10 explain that the coast of Manasseh was on the north side of the river Kanah and that the sea was the northern border of Manasseh.

questions.question: Which territory on the border of Manasseh was actually allocated to the children of Ephraim?
options: Tappuah
Michmethah
Bethshean
Entappuah
questions.correctAnswer: Tappuah
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:8 states that while Manasseh had the land of Tappuah, Tappuah on the border belonged to the children of Ephraim.

questions.question: What challenge did the children of Manasseh face in the cities of Issachar and Asher?
options: They could not drive out the inhabitants
They were attacked by neighboring tribes
They lost their inheritance
They were blessed with abundant crops
questions.correctAnswer: They could not drive out the inhabitants
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:12 clearly states that the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities and that the Canaanites would dwell in the land.

questions.question: How does Joshua 17:12-13 teach about faith and obedience in facing difficult circumstances?
options: Faith leads to complete victory over enemies
Obedience may require enduring partial presence of adversaries
God abandons those who fail to obey
Canaanites were to be destroyed immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience may require enduring partial presence of adversaries
questions.explanation: Verses 12 and 13 show that although the children of Manasseh could not completely drive out the Canaanites, they put them to tribute, illustrating that obedience and faith sometimes involve perseverance despite incomplete victory.

questions.question: What advice did Joshua give to the children of Joseph when they complained about their inheritance?
options: Take the land of the Perizzites and giants by force
Accept the smaller portion quietly
Share the land with Ephraim
Seek another inheritance beyond Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: Take the land of the Perizzites and giants by force
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:15 records Joshua telling the children of Joseph to go into the wood country and cut down for themselves in the land of the Perizzites and giants if the land of Ephraim was too narrow.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 17:7, the border of Manasseh extended to the inhabitants of Entappuah on its right hand.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:7 specifically states that the border went along on the right hand unto the inhabitants of Entappuah, confirming the answer as True.

questions.question: Which cities and their towns did Manasseh have in Issachar and Asher as mentioned in Joshua 17?
options: Bethshean, Ibleam, Dor, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo
Jericho, Ai, Bethel, Hebron, Shechem
Gilead, Bashan, Michmethah, Entappuah
Tappuah, Kanah, Ephraim, Perizzites
questions.correctAnswer: Bethshean, Ibleam, Dor, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:11 lists these cities and their towns as part of Manasseh's inheritance in Issachar and Asher.

questions.question: What is the significance of the iron chariots mentioned in Joshua 17:16 for the children of Joseph?
options: They represented a military challenge the children of Joseph feared
They were gifts from the Canaanites
They symbolized peace between tribes
They were used by the children of Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: They represented a military challenge the children of Joseph feared
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:16 mentions that the Canaanites dwelling in the valley had iron chariots, which implied a strong military advantage that concerned the children of Joseph.

questions.question: Joshua 17:17-18 promises what outcome if the children of Joseph cut down the wood and drive out the Canaanites?
options: They will possess the mountain and its outgoings despite the strength of Canaanites
They will be defeated by iron chariots
They will only have one portion of land
They will form an alliance with the Canaanites
questions.correctAnswer: They will possess the mountain and its outgoings despite the strength of Canaanites
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:17-18 encourages that the mountain shall be theirs if they cut down the wood and drive out the Canaanites, even though the Canaanites have iron chariots and are strong.

questions.question: What does Joshua 17:14 reveal about the children of Joseph's perception of their assigned inheritance?
options: They thought it was too small for their large population
They were content with one lot and one portion
They wanted to share with the tribe of Ephraim
They requested no inheritance
questions.correctAnswer: They thought it was too small for their large population
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:14 shows that the children of Joseph felt that one lot and one portion was insufficient given that the Lord had blessed them and they were a great people.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua told the children of Joseph that they would only receive one lot of land regardless of their size.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:17 contradicts this by stating that the children of Joseph would not have just one lot but would also receive the mountain and its outgoings, showing that the answer is False.

questions.question: How does the passage in Joshua 17:12-13 teach about dealing with incomplete victories and the presence of opposition?
options: It shows that God allows opposition to remain for disciplinary purposes
It encourages giving up when faced with strong enemies
It illustrates that partial victory with tribute is possible while maintaining faith
It suggests making peace treaties immediately
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates that partial victory with tribute is possible while maintaining faith
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 describe how the children of Manasseh could not drive out all inhabitants but put them to tribute, teaching that faith involves persevering and trusting God even when victory is not total.

questions.question: What does Joshua 17:10 indicate about the meeting point of the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh?
options: They met at Asher on the north and Issachar on the east
They met at Michmethah
They met at the Jordan River
They met at the city of Tappuah
questions.correctAnswer: They met at Asher on the north and Issachar on the east
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:10 states that Ephraim and Manasseh met together in Asher on the north and in Issachar on the east.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 17:6, the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance equal to that of the sons.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:6 clearly states that the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons, confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: Based on Joshua 17:7-8, how does the passage highlight the complexity of tribal borders and inheritance?
options: Borders often overlapped with cities belonging to other tribes
All borders were clearly defined without dispute
No cities belonged to more than one tribe
Tribal inheritance was uniform and simple
questions.correctAnswer: Borders often overlapped with cities belonging to other tribes
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:7-8 shows that Manasseh's borders included cities like Tappuah, but some cities on the border belonged to Ephraim, illustrating overlapping territorial claims.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 17.

questions.question: What was the reason given for Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh, receiving Gilead and Bashan?
options: Because he was a man of war
Because he was the youngest son
Because he was a priest
Because he requested it
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was a man of war
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:1 states that Machir had Gilead and Bashan because he was a man of war.

questions.question: Who approached Eleazar, Joshua, and the princes to claim an inheritance among their brethren?
options: The daughters of Zelophehad
The sons of Manasseh
The children of Ephraim
The priests of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The daughters of Zelophehad
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:4 explains that Zelophehad's daughters came before Eleazar, Joshua, and the princes to claim their inheritance as commanded by the LORD.

questions.question: How many portions fell to Manasseh besides the land of Gilead and Bashan?
options: Ten
Five
Seven
Twelve
questions.correctAnswer: Ten
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:5 specifies that ten portions fell to Manasseh besides the land of Gilead and Bashan.

questions.question: Which tribe had the city of Tappuah on the border, though the city belonged to another tribe?
options: Manasseh had Tappuah, but it belonged to Ephraim
Ephraim had Tappuah, but it belonged to Manasseh
Judah had Tappuah, but it belonged to Manasseh
Manasseh had Tappuah, but it belonged to Issachar
questions.correctAnswer: Manasseh had Tappuah, but it belonged to Ephraim
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:8 states that Manasseh had the land of Tappuah, but Tappuah on the border belonged to the children of Ephraim.

questions.question: Which cities and their towns did Manasseh have in Issachar and Asher?
options: Bethshean, Ibleam, Dor, Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo
Bethel, Shechem, Hebron, and Jericho
Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, and Ekron
Jerusalem, Bethlehem, and Hebron
questions.correctAnswer: Bethshean, Ibleam, Dor, Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:11 lists these cities and their towns as those Manasseh had in Issachar and Asher.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Manasseh were able to completely drive out the Canaanites from their allotted cities.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:12 clearly states that the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities, and the Canaanites still dwelt there.

questions.question: What did the children of Israel do to the Canaanites when they became strong?
options: Put them to tribute but did not utterly drive them out
Completely destroyed them
Made peace treaties with them
Ignored them
questions.correctAnswer: Put them to tribute but did not utterly drive them out
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:13 explains that Israel put the Canaanites to tribute but did not fully drive them out.

questions.question: What complaint did the children of Joseph make to Joshua regarding their inheritance?
options: They received only one lot and one portion despite being a great people
They were given too much land
Their land was poor and barren
They were not given any land
questions.correctAnswer: They received only one lot and one portion despite being a great people
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:14 records the children of Joseph asking why they received only one lot and one portion, despite being a great people blessed by the LORD.

questions.question: What did Joshua suggest the children of Joseph do if the land of Mount Ephraim was too narrow for them?
options: Go to the wood country and cut down trees in the land of the Perizzites and giants
Request more land from the other tribes
Migrate to another country
Build cities in the valley
questions.correctAnswer: Go to the wood country and cut down trees in the land of the Perizzites and giants
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:15 states Joshua's advice to cut down trees in the land of the Perizzites and giants if Mount Ephraim was too narrow.

questions.question: Why did the children of Joseph say the hill country was not enough for them?
options: Because the Canaanites in the valley had iron chariots
Because the hills were barren
Because they disliked mountainous terrain
Because they lacked water sources
questions.correctAnswer: Because the Canaanites in the valley had iron chariots
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:16 explains their concern that the hills were insufficient as the Canaanites in the valley had iron chariots.

questions.question: How did Joshua respond to the house of Joseph regarding the number of lots they would receive?
options: They would not have only one lot but the mountain would be theirs
They would only have one lot
They would share lots with Ephraim
They would receive no lots
questions.correctAnswer: They would not have only one lot but the mountain would be theirs
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:17-18 states Joshua told them they would not have only one lot; the mountain would belong to them, and they should cut down the wood and drive out the Canaanites.

questions.question: What is the significance of the term 'iron chariots' mentioned in Joshua 17:16 and 17:18?
options: It symbolizes military strength and technological advantage of the Canaanites
It refers to ceremonial vehicles used in worship
It means chariots made of bronze
It is a metaphor for spiritual power
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes military strength and technological advantage of the Canaanites
questions.explanation: The phrase 'iron chariots' in Joshua 17:16 and 17:18 refers to the superior military technology that made the Canaanites formidable foes.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage corresponds to the theme of daughters inheriting land when no sons are present, as seen with Zelophehad's daughters in Joshua 17?
options: Numbers 27:1-11
Genesis 12:1-3
Exodus 20:1-17
Deuteronomy 6:4-9
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 27:1-11
questions.explanation: Numbers 27:1-11 records the initial petition and command of inheritance for Zelophehad's daughters, which Joshua 17:3-4 fulfills.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua's instruction to the children of Joseph to cut down the wood and drive out the Canaanites foreshadows Israel's later complete conquest of the land under King David and Solomon.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:18 foreshadows the eventual complete conquest and settlement of Israel, which historical accounts such as 2 Samuel and 1 Kings describe under David and Solomon.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in Joshua 17:14-18 where Joshua challenges the children of Joseph to expand their territory by cutting down the wood and driving out the Canaanites?
options: Inclusio highlighting a challenge and promise
Chiasm emphasizing the central theme
Parallelism contrasting tribes
Allegory representing spiritual warfare
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio highlighting a challenge and promise
questions.explanation: The passage forms an inclusio framing the challenge of limited land with the promise of expansion, motivating the children of Joseph to action.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Joshua 17:1 reveal about God's blessing and the nature of Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh?
options: Machir was blessed for his wisdom and received Gilead and Bashan
Machir was a man of war and therefore was given Gilead and Bashan
Machir was a priest and thus was given the land of Shechem
Machir was the youngest son and received no inheritance
questions.correctAnswer: Machir was a man of war and therefore was given Gilead and Bashan
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:1 states that because Machir was a man of war, he had Gilead and Bashan, showing God's blessing on his military prowess and leadership.

questions.question: According to Joshua 17:3-4, what doctrine concerning inheritance and gender is established by the daughters of Zelophehad?
options: Only sons can inherit land in Israel
Daughters can inherit if there are no sons, as commanded by the LORD
Inheritance is given only to priests
Inheritance is divided equally among all children regardless of gender
questions.correctAnswer: Daughters can inherit if there are no sons, as commanded by the LORD
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 4 explain that Zelophehad’s daughters received an inheritance because the LORD commanded Moses to give them land among their brethren due to the absence of sons, teaching a principle of inheritance by daughters in absence of male heirs.

questions.question: What theological insight about God's justice and faithfulness is reflected in the division of land to Manasseh as described in Joshua 17:5-6?
options: God arbitrarily distributed land without regard to family size
God gave no inheritance to the tribe of Manasseh
God ensured daughters received inheritance and sons received additional land, showing fairness
God only gave land to the tribe of Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: God ensured daughters received inheritance and sons received additional land, showing fairness
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 indicate that the daughters received an inheritance among the sons, and the sons had the land of Gilead, demonstrating God's just and faithful distribution of land according to His command.

questions.question: In Joshua 17:7-10, how is God's providence revealed through the detailed boundaries of Manasseh's inheritance?
options: God gave Manasseh a small, insignificant portion
God established clear and expansive borders including both mountain and sea boundaries
God gave Manasseh only cities within Ephraim’s territory
God left the borders of Manasseh undefined
questions.correctAnswer: God established clear and expansive borders including both mountain and sea boundaries
questions.explanation: Verses 7-10 describe detailed borders from Asher to Michmethah and to the sea, showing God's providential care in defining Manasseh’s inheritance precisely and expansively.

questions.question: What doctrinal lesson about human responsibility and spiritual warfare is taught in Joshua 17:12-13 regarding the Canaanites dwelling in the land?
options: Israelites drove out all the Canaanites without difficulty
The presence of Canaanites shows Israel’s failure to fully obey and drive out all enemies
God promised Israel they would never face enemies in the land
The Canaanites were allies of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The presence of Canaanites shows Israel’s failure to fully obey and drive out all enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 reveal that Israel could not drive out the Canaanites completely but put them to tribute, illustrating the ongoing spiritual battle and human responsibility in obedience to God’s commands.

questions.question: What does the complaint of the children of Joseph in Joshua 17:14 teach about human perspective on divine provision?
options: They were content with the land allotted
They questioned the sufficiency of their inheritance despite being a great people
They refused to accept any land
They asked for a double portion of land
questions.correctAnswer: They questioned the sufficiency of their inheritance despite being a great people
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:14 shows the children of Joseph expressing dissatisfaction with their single lot, reflecting human concerns about adequacy despite God's blessings.

questions.question: How does Joshua's response in Joshua 17:15 demonstrate the principle of sanctification and active faith?
options: He encourages them to passively wait for more land
He commands them to cut down the forest and take the land from giants, showing active faith and sanctification
He gives them more land immediately without effort
He tells them to abandon their claim
questions.correctAnswer: He commands them to cut down the forest and take the land from giants, showing active faith and sanctification
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:15 instructs the people to actively claim and sanctify the land by cutting down the wood and driving out enemies, illustrating the call to active faith and holiness.

questions.question: What theological significance is found in the mention of 'chariots of iron' in Joshua 17:16 regarding divine power and human limitation?
options: The Israelites had more iron chariots than the Canaanites
The presence of iron chariots symbolizes strong enemies, yet God empowers Israel to overcome
Iron chariots were irrelevant to the battle
The Canaanites were weak and insignificant
questions.correctAnswer: The presence of iron chariots symbolizes strong enemies, yet God empowers Israel to overcome
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:16 highlights the military strength of the Canaanites, implying that human strength alone is insufficient and pointing to God’s power in enabling victory despite formidable foes.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth about God’s promise and human responsibility is taught by Joshua 17:17-18 in relation to the house of Joseph?
options: God promises land but requires the people to actively drive out enemies despite difficulties
God gives land without any human effort
God forbids the house of Joseph from expanding their territory
The house of Joseph will never overcome the Canaanites
questions.correctAnswer: God promises land but requires the people to actively drive out enemies despite difficulties
questions.explanation: Verses 17-18 combine the promise of land to a great and powerful people with the command to drive out the strong Canaanites, teaching the balance of divine promise and human responsibility in sanctification.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in His command to give daughters an inheritance in Joshua 17:4?
options: God’s wrath
God’s justice and faithfulness
God’s wrathful judgment
God’s silence
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice and faithfulness
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:4 shows God’s justice and faithfulness by ensuring the daughters receive inheritance as commanded to Moses, upholding righteousness in property rights.

questions.question: How does the land allocation in Joshua 17:11 reveal God's providence in the fulfillment of His covenant promises?
options: God gave Manasseh control over significant cities in Issachar and Asher, fulfilling territorial promises
God gave Manasseh no land at all
God gave all land to the Canaanites
God only promised land to the tribe of Levi
questions.correctAnswer: God gave Manasseh control over significant cities in Issachar and Asher, fulfilling territorial promises
questions.explanation: Verse 11 details Manasseh’s possession of key cities, demonstrating God's providential faithfulness to fulfill His promises of land to the tribes of Israel.

questions.question: What does Joshua 17:8-9 teach about the complexity of tribal boundaries and God's sovereign control over Israel's inheritance?
options: Tribal boundaries were simple and identical
Tribal boundaries overlapped, showing God's sovereign orchestration despite complexities
Ephraim had no land
All land belonged to Manasseh exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: Tribal boundaries overlapped, showing God's sovereign orchestration despite complexities
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 show that Tappuah belonged to Ephraim though it was within Manasseh’s land, illustrating God's sovereign and purposeful arrangement of boundaries.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s command to drive out Canaanites was unjust and cruel. How does Joshua 17:12-13 clarify the actual biblical teaching on this issue?
options: God commanded total extermination without any allowance for mercy
Israel was not able to fully drive out the Canaanites and made them tributaries, showing restraint and partial judgment
God ignored the presence of Canaanites
Israel cohabited peacefully with all Canaanites
questions.correctAnswer: Israel was not able to fully drive out the Canaanites and made them tributaries, showing restraint and partial judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 show Israel’s incomplete conquest and the continued presence of Canaanites as tributaries, indicating God’s judgment was purposeful and allowed for human responsibility and consequences.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Joshua 17:14-15 reveal about the transition from wilderness wanderings to conquest and possession?
options: Israel remained in the wilderness indefinitely
Israel begins to actively claim and conquer the land promised to their forefathers
Conquest was given without any warfare
Israel rejected the promised land
questions.correctAnswer: Israel begins to actively claim and conquer the land promised to their forefathers
questions.explanation: These verses show Israel moving from receiving land by lot to actively cutting down forests and fighting giants, marking the fulfillment of God’s promise in the conquest phase.

questions.question: Combining Joshua 17:1 and Joshua 17:11, what theological insight emerges about the role of divine empowerment and human inheritance in God’s plan?
options: Inheritance is given randomly without regard to ability
Divine empowerment as a man of war led to receiving strategic territories and cities, showing God’s blessing on strength for His purposes
Inheritance is only spiritual, not physical
The tribe of Manasseh received no cities or land
questions.correctAnswer: Divine empowerment as a man of war led to receiving strategic territories and cities, showing God’s blessing on strength for His purposes
questions.explanation: Joshua 17:1 states Machir was given land due to being a man of war, and 17:11 lists cities under Manasseh’s control, illustrating God’s blessing and empowerment for fulfilling His covenant.
